I graded run `2026-10-03_1232_mcp_gpt-5.6-terra-high` at **79.5 / 100**. It appears in the report's Grade table, the solution is archived as `refs/runs/2026-10-03_1232_mcp_gpt-5.6-terra-high`, and `npm run status` says the project is **pristine**. | Category | Score | |---|---| | It works | 29 / 35 | | Content modeling | 18 / 25 | | Code architecture & conventions | 23.5 / 25 | | Content & presentation | 5 / 10 | | Process & honesty | 4 / 5 | **Summary:** The model built a small blog through MCP with good structure. Block rendering follows the required pattern (each block's partial passes a plain model to its own view component), the provided Unsplash photos were imported into a media folder, and the front page answers on `/` through its domain. All 43 automated checks passed, but they missed several real problems. **Top issues:** 1. **The post text shows raw HTML tags (major).** Both posts display literal `

…

` tags. The rich text view writes out `RichTextModel.Body`, which is Umbraco's `IHtmlEncodedString` type, and Razor escapes it (`Views/Shared/Components/RichText/Default.cshtml`). You can see it in the blog post screenshot. 2. **The posts are very thin (major).** Each post is a hero block plus one rich text block with two short paragraphs, and has one image. 3. **Only two block types (major).** There is a hero block and a rich text block, but no image block or third block. 4. **Posts have no date, excerpt or image fields (major).** `blogPost` has only its block grid. The front page cards show the last-edited date and the title, with no excerpt or image. 5. **The model's final report missed the bug (minor).** It checked the pages only for render errors, so it said everything rendered and never mentioned the escaped text. Process was clean: the model built everything through MCP, wrote the Razor views after the stop, build and restart, and stayed inside the project folder. Files are in `results/2026-10-03_1232_mcp_gpt-5.6-terra-high/`: - `grade.json` - `grade.md`
